title: The Euler Product and Its Convergence Boundary
mathematical_role: Expose prime-indexed local factors, their infinite product, and the Re(s)>1 absolute-convergence boundary explicitly.
learning_objective: Understand both the local-to-global Euler product and why its convergence domain must remain visible.
literal_semantics: The Euler product is indexed by all primes and expresses unique prime factorization analytically in its half-plane of absolute convergence.
The product implies zeta(s) is nonzero for Re(s)>1.
nonliteral_semantics: The product is not licensed for term-by-term manipulation inside the critical strip.
Analytic continuation beyond Re(s)>1 is a separate analytic construction.

notes: Candidate semantics are bounded by the existing documentary source; no new mathematical source is admitted by this visual operation.

accessibility.alt_text: Prime-indexed Euler factors for p equals 2, 3, 5, and all primes assemble into the zeta Euler product, with Re(s) greater than 1 marked as the absolute-convergence domain.
accessibility.long_description: Four local-factor boxes feed into the exact Euler-product formula. A prominent boundary states Re(s)>1. Lower panels distinguish what the convergent product proves there from what it does not authorize inside the critical strip.
